Από τη Θεσσαλονίκη προς τα Δυτικά Βαλκάνια ένας ενεργειακός "κάθετος διάδρομος" με εμπορική και περιφερειακή σημασία.
Δυναμικό "παρών" στην 90ή Διεθνή Έκθεση Θεσσαλονίκης έδωσε το Ταμείο Επαγγελματικής Ασφάλισης Υπαλλήλων Φαρμακευτικών Εργασιών (Τ.Ε.Α.Υ.Φ.Ε.), επιβεβαιώνοντας τη σταθερή στρατηγική εξωστρέφειας που ακολουθεί και ενισχύοντας περαιτέρω τη θεσμική του παρουσία.
Το Ταμείο εκπροσώπησαν ο πρόεδρος του Διοικητικού Συμβουλίου κ. Ελευθέριος Ντούμας, το μέλος του Δ.Σ. κ. Βασίλης Καραχισαρίδης και η Γενική Διευθύντρια του Τ.Ε.Α.Υ.Φ.Ε. κα Αργυρώ Παπαναγιώτου, οι οποίοι κατά τη διάρκεια της ΔΕΘ είχαν σειρά ουσιαστικών επαφών με την πολιτική ηγεσία, φορείς της κοινωνικής ασφάλισης και της δημόσιας διοίκησης, καθώς και με εκπροσώπους του ευρύτερου φαρμακευτικού κλάδου.
Ιδιαίτερη βαρύτητα είχαν οι συναντήσεις με την Υπουργό Εργασίας και Κοινωνικής Ασφάλισης κα Νίκη Κεραμέως, την Υφυπουργό Εργασίας και Κοινωνικής Ασφάλισης κα Άννα Ευθυμίου και τον Γενικό Γραμματέα Κοινωνικών Ασφαλίσεων κ. Κωνσταντίνο Τσαγκαρόπουλο.
Οι επαφές αυτές αποτέλεσαν ευκαιρία για άμεση επικοινωνία με την πολιτική ηγεσία του Υπουργείου Εργασίας και Κοινωνικής Ασφάλισης και για ουσιαστική ανταλλαγή απόψεων σχετικά με τις εξελίξεις στον χώρο της κοινωνικής και επαγγελματικής ασφάλισης, τις σύγχρονες προκλήσεις που αντιμετωπίζουν οι ασφαλιστικοί φορείς, καθώς και τις προοπτικές περαιτέρω ανάπτυξης και εκσυγχρονισμού του Τ.Ε.Α.Υ.Φ.Ε.
Στον κύκλο των θεσμικών επαφών περιλαμβάνονταν και στελέχη της Διοίκησης του e-ΕΦΚΑ, με τα οποία συζητήθηκαν ζητήματα κοινού ενδιαφέροντος που αφορούν την κοινωνική ασφάλιση και τη λειτουργία των ασφαλιστικών φορέων.
Έμφαση δόθηκε και στις εξελίξεις στον τομέα της ψηφιακής διακυβέρνησης, με αναφορά στις πρωτοβουλίες και τις κατευθύνσεις του Υπουργείου Ψηφιακής Διακυβέρνησης για τον ψηφιακό μετασχηματισμό και την ενίσχυση της διαλειτουργικότητας των ασφαλιστικών υπηρεσιών. Σχετική συνάντηση πραγματοποιήθηκε με τη Διευθύνουσα Σύμβουλο της Ηλεκτρονικής Διακυβέρνησης Υγείας και Κοινωνικής Ασφάλισης (ΗΔΙΚΑ) κα Νίκη Τσούμα, με επίκεντρο ζητήματα που συνδέονται με τον εκσυγχρονισμό και την αποτελεσματικότερη λειτουργία των υπηρεσιών του ασφαλιστικού τομέα.
Τα στελέχη του Τ.Ε.Α.Υ.Φ.Ε. είχαν ακόμη την ευκαιρία να ενημερωθούν άμεσα για τις κυβερνητικές κατευθύνσεις και τις επικείμενες παρεμβάσεις στον τομέα της κοινωνικής ασφάλισης, με έμφαση σε ζητήματα ασφαλιστικών εισφορών, συνταξιοδοτικών παροχών, προστασίας ασφαλισμένων και συνταξιούχων, καθώς και στις ευρύτερες μεταρρυθμίσεις που επηρεάζουν τη λειτουργία και τις προοπτικές των ασφαλιστικών φορέων.
Στον ευρύτερο χώρο του Φαρμάκου, πραγματοποιήθηκε συνάντηση με τον Πρόεδρο του Εθνικού Οργανισμού Φαρμάκων (ΕΟΦ) κ. Σπυρίδωνα Σαπουνά, ενισχύοντας τον διάλογο του Ταμείου με θεσμικούς φορείς που συνδέονται άμεσα με τον κλάδο.
Ακολούθησαν επαφές με εκπροσώπους και στελέχη φαρμακευτικών επιχειρήσεων, μεταξύ των οποίων ο Αναπληρωτής Πρόεδρος του Συνδέσμου Φαρμακευτικών Επιχειρήσεων Ελλάδος (ΣΦΕΕ) και Αντιπρόεδρος της ΒΙΑΝΕΞ Α.Ε. κ. Κωνσταντίνος Παναγούλιας, καθώς και ο Αντιπρόεδρος του Διοικητικού Συμβουλίου και Διευθύνων Σύμβουλος της Win Medica κ. Χρήστος Σωτηρίου.
Ο κύκλος των επαφών στον χώρο του Φαρμάκου διευρύνθηκε με μέλη του Πανελλήνιου Φαρμακευτικού Συλλόγου και του Πανελλήνιου Κτηνιατρικού Συλλόγου, καθώς και με εκπροσώπους Ομοσπονδιών, Συλλόγων και φορέων εργαζομένων από όλη την Ελλάδα. Η ανταλλαγή απόψεων επικεντρώθηκε σε ζητήματα που απασχολούν τον κλάδο και τους εργαζομένους του, ενισχύοντας παράλληλα την επικοινωνία του Ταμείου με φορείς που συνδέονται άμεσα με τους ασφαλισμένους του.
Κατά τη διάρκεια των επαφών, ο Πρόεδρος του Τ.Ε.Α.Υ.Φ.Ε. κ. Ελευθέριος Ντούμας αναφέρθηκε στην πορεία και στις προτεραιότητες του Ταμείου, επισημαίνοντας τη συστηματική προσπάθεια που καταβάλλεται για την ενίσχυση της οικονομικής του ευρωστίας, την διασφάλιση της μακροχρόνιας βιωσιμότητάς του και τον συνεχή εκσυγχρονισμό της λειτουργίας και των υπηρεσιών του.
Αναφορά έγινε επίσης στη διαρκή συνεργασία του Τ.Ε.Α.Υ.Φ.Ε. με τους αρμόδιους θεσμικούς και εποπτικούς φορείς και στη σταθερή προσήλωση της Διοίκησης και των εργαζομένων στη συνεχή αναβάθμιση της λειτουργίας του.
Ο κ. Ντούμας υπογράμμισε ότι το Τ.Ε.Α.Υ.Φ.Ε. θα συνεχίσει με συνέπεια την προσπάθεια για τη λειτουργική και οικονομική του ενίσχυση και τον περαιτέρω εκσυγχρονισμό των υπηρεσιών του, με σταθερό προσανατολισμό στην προάσπιση των συμφερόντων και των δικαιωμάτων των ασφαλισμένων και των συνταξιούχων του.
Η συμμετοχή του Τ.Ε.Α.Υ.Φ.Ε. στην 90ή Διεθνή Έκθεση Θεσσαλονίκης ανέδειξε την σταθερή επιλογή του Ταμείου για ουσιαστικό θεσμικό διάλογο, διεύρυνση των συνεργασιών του και ενεργό συμμετοχή στις εξελίξεις που αφορούν την κοινωνική και επαγγελματική ασφάλιση και τον ευρύτερο χώρο του Φαρμάκου.

title: How poorly fitted sports bras drive girls out of sports
content:
How poorly fitted sports bras drive girls out of careers
What you need to know:
- Poorly fitted sports bras can cause pain, discomfort and embarrassment, yet schools and sports organisations rarely provide proper breast support.
- Researchers say recognising sports bras as essential sports equipment could improve comfort, confidence and performance.
Australian sport has a participation problem, especially when it comes to girls and women. In fact, Australian girls and women are dropping out of organised sports at concerning rates. There are myriad reasons why this is happening. One barrier that gets little coverage is sports bras.
We recently studied how decision-makers in schools and sports organisations understand breast-related barriers to participation and whether they recognised sports bras as part of the solution.
Why are sports bras so important?
Sports bras are essential for girls and women because breasts move a lot during activities such as running, jumping or quick changes in direction. This movement can cause pain, chafing and embarrassment, which may discourage participation and hurt performance.
A high-support, properly fitted sports bra can alleviate or resolve these issues and allow girls and women to exercise comfortably. However, research shows up to 88 per cent of girls wear sports bras that do not fit properly and only about a third wear a sports bra during PE or school sports.
Not including sports bras in school uniforms or sports kits, and not teaching about bra fit and breast health, are gaps that need addressing. The good news is these gaps can be addressed through practical, achievable changes to assist the health, comfort and performance of girls and women playing sport.
We identified several problems
Our team surveyed 225 people – including coaches, teachers, administrators and programme coordinators – who decide on sports kit items in 153 sporting organisations and 72 schools across Australia.
We identified several key issues: many girls and women do not understand the benefits of supportive sports bras; cost makes it difficult for some to access sports bras, especially in schools and community sports; and sports bras are often seen as underwear instead of performance equipment.
One respondent told us: “In the same way that a mouth guard protects teeth, breasts are high-contact areas in our sport that require protection and support.”
Most respondents said breast-related issues negatively affect participation – a majority believed about 40 per cent of girls and women in their organisations faced breast-related problems that limited participation, led to dropping out and impacted performance.
However, most understood the benefits of sports bras: about 95 per cent believed sports bras help prevent breast pain during exercise, and more than 90 per cent said they reduced embarrassment from too much breast movement.
About 92 per cent of decision-makers thought girls and women would benefit from learning about sports bra design, fit and support. While two-thirds felt their organisation should provide this education, less than one per cent actually offered sports bra education. Only two per cent formally included sports bras in school or sports kits.
We also suggest some solutions
We developed a guide that presents solutions to assist sports and schools in dealing with this problem. It includes facts, free evidence-based resources on sports bras for use in promotional efforts, and case studies on organisations that are educating and supporting girls and women to access sports bras.
Key solutions included schools and sports accepting the responsibility to educate girls and women on the importance of wearing supportive, well-fitted sports bras and recognising sports bras as an essential item in sports kits.
Two case studies also identified recent success stories: At Gilgandra High School in New South Wales, teachers noticed few girls were taking part in sports and found a lack of access to supportive sports bras was a problem. The school used NSW government equity funding to give students professionally fitted sports bras for free.
Also read: What if the bra lets her down?
This led to a 35 per cent increase in girls taking part in the school’s athletics carnival. It also boosted their confidence, comfort and willingness to talk about breast health. Also, the Queensland Academy of Sport added breast health education and sports bra fittings to their athlete support services. A physiotherapist met with athletes one-on-one to explain how sports bra design and fit can improve performance and comfort and help prevent breast injuries.
The academy found its athletes were much more likely to use breast health resources after getting personal advice from trusted health professionals. These sessions also made it easier to talk about breast health and lowered barriers to getting help.
Practical tips for sports and schools
There are several things sporting clubs and schools can do to help: Recognise sports bras as essential equipment for girls and women because breast support is important for keeping them involved in sport; add breast health and sports bra education, along with access to evidence-based resources, to physical education programmes in high schools and women’s sport training sessions; offer opportunities for girls and women to learn about sports bra design and proper fit in supportive settings; and assist with funding or identify where funding could be provided to help make sports bras more affordable.
If we want to boost participation and reduce dropout rates among girls and women, making sure they have access to proper breast support could be one of the easiest and most effective things we do.
Deirdre McGhee is a researcher and senior lecturer at the University of Wollongong and APA sports physiotherapist at the University of Wollongong; Clare Hanlon is a professor and chairperson of Susan Alberti Women in Sport at Victoria University; and Dr Elliott Flowers is a postdoctoral research fellow (Women and Girls in Sport), Victoria University.

title: Diesel refunds set to exit the VAT system
content:
Standalone refund system promises greater visibility, with both users and sellers required to register.
The South African Revenue Service (Sars) is introducing a new standalone diesel refund system that is being developed separately from the value-added tax (VAT) system. It forms part of Sars’s excise modernisation project.
All existing and new users will have to re-register on the new system, with the registration process starting on Monday (21 September).
In a significant change, both users and sellers of diesel will have to register, rather than only users. Claims for diesel purchased from a seller who is not registered with Sars will not qualify.
At a high level, there are certainly some positives to the new system, says Amanda Nkwanyana, a partner in the Webber Wentzel tax team.
“A standalone diesel refund system should, in principle, simplify administration and give both Sars and taxpayers greater visibility over registrations and claims. The move away from claiming through the VAT system may also create a more dedicated process for diesel refunds.”
Rules and rollout
Senior Sars officials on Friday shed light on the new system, the rules and the rollout process over the next couple of months.
The first phase is the registration of users and sellers.
Another change is the inclusion of contractors operating on a wet basis. Mahlatse Ledwaba, an excise specialist at Sars, says that under the current system only entities that purchase diesel for their own use qualify for the rebate.
Under the new system, contractors operating on behalf of other entities will also become eligible.
In terms of the new legislation, the qualifying categories are grouped into eight industries: agriculture (formerly farming and forestry), fishing, mining on land, offshore mining and offshore shipping, harbour shipping, rail freight transport, and electricity generation.
Registration applications can be submitted via eFiling or by booking an appointment at a branch office.
“Specific supporting documents, depending on the category, will be required and can be uploaded on the eFiling system.”
Ledwaba says applicants will receive an acknowledgement letter, a case number and a letter informing them of the outcome of their registration.
She stresses that until a “go-live date” has been announced, claims will continue to be submitted through the current system.
Deshen Pillay, a member of the team designing the electronic registration solution, says the registration process is split into three phases, with the registration of users and sellers as the starting phase.
The next phase will require users and sellers to declare their relationships to Sars. Nkwanyana says it appears that Sars intends to create a verified relationship between diesel sellers and users so that it can better monitor transactions and validate future claims.
Unanswered questions
“That being said, there are still a number of important practical questions that remain unanswered,” says Nkwanyana.
“Many taxpayers purchase diesel from multiple suppliers, but there was very little detail on how those multiple supplier relationships will be managed in practice, what administrative burden this may create, and what happens if one of those suppliers falls out of compliance.”
Another notable gap, she says, relates to logbooks and supporting records.
“Historically, the adequacy of logbooks and diesel usage records has been one of the biggest areas of dispute between Sars and taxpayers during diesel refund audits.”
She notes that the Sars webinar did not provide much detail on whether the substantiation requirements will change under the new system or how Sars intends to deal with these longstanding issues.
Ledwaba says there will be follow-up information sessions to inform taxpayers of all the requirements and assist them with the process as the system is rolled out.
The third phase will involve setting up users’ profiles. This will include their qualifying activities, site plans showing where the activities are performed, the equipment used, and the applicable licences and permits.
“This part is still under development and will only be implemented early next year. This will be in preparation for the second project, which is the actual claim functionality,” Pillay said during the webinar.
Key benefits
Chetan Vanmali, a leading indirect tax specialist at Webber Wentzel, identifies four key benefits:
- Improved transparency: Standalone administration should provide users with clearer visibility of registrations, claims, verifications and refund status.
- Better compliance and reduced fraud: Electronic registration, automated checks and seller-user relationship validation should strengthen compliance and reduce fraud.
- Faster processing: If Sars’s technology performs as intended, dedicated processing should allow diesel claims to be dealt with independently of Vat verifications and assessments.
- More predictable cash flow: Separating diesel refunds from Vat may reduce situations where diesel refund issues affect Vat refunds, or vice versa.
Since a large number of users and sellers must be registered and onboarded, the registration process has opened several months before the claim submission functionality becomes operational, Pillay says.
“This is to afford Sars sufficient time to onboard everyone and to be ready when the claim submission system is implemented,” he adds.
The new diesel refund system will only become effective once the claim submission functionality is implemented. Until then, claims will continue to be submitted through the existing Vat system.

title: Varenicline and combination nicotine replacement therapy deemed preferred treatments for tobacco use
content:
A new clinical practice guideline from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and Department of Defense (DoD) provides recommendations for tobacco use treatment. Tobacco and nicotine use among veterans and military service members causes physical and mental health effects and reduces force readiness.
The guideline, published in the Annals of Internal Medicine, recommends varenicline or combination nicotine replacement therapy for cessation and emphasizes the safety and efficacy of pharmacotherapy for patients with mental health conditions. An editorial and a synopsis are also published in the same journal issue.
VA and DoD convened a multidisciplinary panel to review research published between 2014 and 2024 and develop an updated clinical practice guideline for tobacco use treatment. The resulting guideline includes 32 recommendations covering smoking cessation medications, counseling approaches and treatment strategies for adults who use a variety of tobacco and nicotine products.
Key recommendations include motivational interviewing to increase engagement in treatment; using varenicline or combination nicotine replacement therapy to increase abstinence; immediate retreatment for individuals who relapse; and offering treatment even to adults who are not yet ready to quit. The guideline concludes that evidence-based medications and counseling remain the most effective tools for tobacco and nicotine cessation.

title: União Europeia propõe barrar menores em redes sociais, jogos online e chatbots
content: A União Europeia prepara uma proposta de lei para restringir o acesso de menores de 15 anos a redes sociais, plataformas de compartilhamento de vídeos, chatbots de inteligência artificial e jogos online. Segundo um rascunho de documento legal obtido pela AFP, o chamado EU KIDS Act impediria que crianças e adolescentes abaixo dessa idade criassem contas de forma autônoma, com regras diferentes conforme a faixa etária e maior participação dos pais. A proposta também prevê que as empresas adotem o princípio de “segurança por design”, com mudanças na forma como os serviços são desenvolvidos para reduzir riscos ao público infantil. Entre as medidas citadas estão a retirada de recursos considerados potencialmente viciantes, como rolagem infinita, notificações artificiais e determinados sistemas de recompensa. A iniciativa ganhou força após a pressão de países, como França e Grécia, e medidas adotadas pela Austrália, que proibiu o acesso de menores de 16 anos a determinadas plataformas. Na União Europeia, porém, a proposta estabelece regras diferentes de acordo com a idade do usuário. A Comissão Europeia também prevê uma taxa de supervisão cobrada das próprias plataformas para financiar a fiscalização. As novas regras devem complementar o Ato de Serviços Digitais (DSA), que já estabelece obrigações para grandes serviços digitais e prevê multas de até 6% do faturamento global anual das empresas. No entanto, o documento cita que as regras vigentes do DSA “não são suficientes” porque falta uma proibição direta e definitiva contra recursos problemáticos e viciantes. A UE ainda planeja lançar um aplicativo de verificação de idade para auxiliar no cumprimento das restrições e impedir que menores acessem serviços classificados como de risco. UE propõe limite de idade gradual A proposta europeia adota uma abordagem diferente da australiana. Enquanto a Austrália estabeleceu uma restrição geral para menores de 16 anos, o projeto da UE prevê níveis de acesso conforme a idade, com diferentes graus de participação dos responsáveis. A partir dos 15 anos, será possível criar uma conta autônoma nos serviços abrangidos pela legislação. Para adolescentes de 13 e 14 anos, o acesso dependerá da autorização dos pais para a criação de “contas introdutórias”, com recursos limitados, controle de tempo de tela e supervisão parental. Já crianças de 3 a 13 anos poderão acessar apenas contas totalmente controladas pelos pais, em serviços classificados como adequados para o público infantil. Responsabilidade das empresas de tecnologia O rascunho estabelece que as regras devem colocar a responsabilidade sobre as empresas de tecnologia, com mecanismos de proteção incorporados aos próprios serviços. Entre as medidas previstas estão: Privacidade por padrão: contas de menores devem ser privadas e as configurações consideradas de maior risco ficam desativadas; Restrição de contato: usuários desconhecidos não poderão entrar em contato com menores; Controle de algoritmos: sistemas de recomendação devem ser ajustados para reduzir a exposição de crianças a conteúdos prejudiciais; Regras específicas: chatbots de IA e jogos online terão diretrizes próprias de proteção para o público infantil. A presidente da Comissão Europeia, Ursula von der Leyen, deve apresentar as diretrizes gerais durante seu discurso anual ao Parlamento Europeu, em Estrasburgo. A apresentação detalhada deve ocorrer posteriormente com a participação de Henna Virkkunen, responsável pela área digital da UE. O projeto ainda não é uma lei. Depois da apresentação, a proposta terá de passar por negociações entre o Parlamento Europeu e os Estados-membros antes de entrar em vigor. title: Sensors, Vol. 26, Pages 5931: Nested Spatiotemporal Anomaly Detection with Semantic Augmentation: A Case Study in Heritage Conservation
content: Cultural heritage (CH) sites are continuously exposed to pressures that can lead to deterioration. Continuous monitoring and anomaly detection (AD) enable early damage detection for preventive conservation. We propose a late-fusion AD framework combining NST-Net, a nested spatiotemporal neural network, with a semantic module encoding expert conservation rules, and evaluate it on five real-world CH monitoring datasets. NST-Net outperforms six state-of-the-art baselines on most sites, achieving, on average, 42% higher Average Precision than the best baseline per site under a synthetic evaluation protocol emphasizing sharp, short-duration anomalies. Dataset length serves as an important performance factor: the combined architecture and preprocessing pipeline particularly benefit longer campaigns, whereas they add little value on shorter ones. NST-Net also requires approximately 13 times less peak memory than baseline detectors, at a higher but still millisecond-scale latency. Further analysis shows that performance depends strongly on anomaly density, type, and severity. The semantic module passes label-free sanity checks and complements NST-Net effectively (complementarity index > 0.87), identifying conservation-relevant events missed by the deep model. These findings support late-fusion statistical–semantic frameworks for AD in CH monitoring.

title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies LIPA as a prognostic hub and ferroptosis regulator in lung adenocarcinoma.
content: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains one of the leading causes of cancer mortality, underscoring the urgent need for biomarkers and therapeutic targets rooted in metabolic reprogramming. By integrating multi-omics analyses with experimental validation, we identified 67 lipid metabolism-related genes dysregulated in LUAD and constructed a five-gene prognostic signature via LASSO regression; lower expression of the signature genes correlated with poor survival. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics revealed cell-type-specific dysregulation of the hub gene LIPA, which was upregulated in monocytes but downregulated in macrophages within the tumor microenvironment. Functional assays demonstrated that LIPA overexpression inhibited tumor proliferation in vitro and suppressed orthotopic tumor growth in vivo, at least in part through a ferroptosis-dependent mechanism involving TXNIP and ALOX5. Virtual screening further identified Castanospermine as a potential LIPA activator; treatment elevated LIPA expression, modulated the CD4+/CD8 + T-cell ratio, and attenuated tumor progression in mice. Collectively, these findings establish LIPA as a critical link between lipid metabolism, ferroptosis, and immune modulation in LUAD, and provide a prognostic signature for risk stratification as well as a candidate compound for targeting lipid metabolic vulnerabilities.

title: Mike Hammer Engages with Families Receiving Humanitarian Aid in Villa Clara
content:
Mike Hammer, the chief of mission at the U.S. Embassy in Cuba, visited the municipality of Corralillo in Villa Clara this past weekend, particularly the town of Quintín Banderas. His visit aimed to connect with families who benefited from U.S. humanitarian aid packages and ensure the assistance reached those in dire need.
The Embassy captured Hammer's visit in a video shared on its X account, under the hashtag #ConCubanosDeAPie. The footage shows Hammer engaging in conversations with the aid recipients inside their homes.
The visuals highlighted the precarious conditions these families face daily. One woman expressed her gratitude to Hammer upon receiving the aid, saying, "I cried so much. The need is overwhelming," and mentioned that before receiving the package, she had nothing left to eat. Another recipient shared her experience trying the sardines included in the food module.
"Being close to Cubans and listening to them is fundamental to our work," the Embassy noted when posting the video, appreciating the families for "opening their homes and welcoming us warmly."
Follow-Up on Aid Distribution in Villa Clara
This visit was a direct follow-up to the distribution that began in Villa Clara on September 10, when 700 food kits and 700 hygiene kits arrived at Abel Santamaría Airport, targeted for families in Quemado de Güines and Rancho Veloz.
Hammer had previously toured the province from September 12 to 14, visiting vulnerable households in Quemado de Güines and the Cotorra neighborhood. He also met with Bishop Arturo González Amador, the director of Cáritas Santa Clara, and dissident Guillermo "Coco" Fariñas, who had been detained on August 31.
Challenges and Future Aid Plans
During that visit, the Cuban regime launched a disinformation campaign against Hammer in Villa Clara, falsely claiming the food was contaminated—a claim publicly refuted by Cáritas.
The aid Hammer oversees is part of a $100 million program announced by the Trump administration for Cuba. Of this, $60 million is directed through the Catholic Church via Cáritas Cuba and Catholic Relief Services, while $40 million is channeled through other independent organizations, bypassing the Cuban state.
On September 16, the Embassy revealed plans to extend aid to five additional provinces: Camagüey, Ciego de Ávila, Cienfuegos, Matanzas, and Pinar del Río. Shortly thereafter, Cáritas Cienfuegos distributed nearly 700 kits in the Lajas municipality.
Scope and Limitations of the Aid Program
The program is expected to benefit between 100,000 and 120,000 families across Cuba, prioritizing elderly individuals living alone, people with disabilities, pregnant or nursing women, and families with children under five.
Bishop González Amador has cautioned, however, that the assistance has clear limitations: "We can only help the most urgent and distressing cases," stressing that "this is not a permanent social assistance project."
Frequently Asked Questions About U.S. Humanitarian Aid in Cuba
What is the goal of Mike Hammer's visit to Villa Clara?
Mike Hammer's visit aimed to ensure that U.S. humanitarian aid reached those in need and to engage with the families who benefited from the aid packages.
How was the aid distributed across Cuba?
The aid is part of a $100 million program, with $60 million distributed through the Catholic Church and $40 million through other independent organizations, prioritizing vulnerable groups throughout the island.
What challenges have been faced during the aid distribution?
The Cuban regime attempted a disinformation campaign claiming the food was contaminated, which was publicly refuted by Cáritas.

title: Indonesia, France partner to elevate aviation safety oversight
content:
Director General of Civil Aviation Lukman F. Laisa stated that cooperation between Indonesia and France has been active since 2019 under a Technical Cooperation Agreement (TCA) covering inspector competency, standardization, and quality management.
"Entering 2026, this cooperation moves into a new phase focused on building a sustainable oversight system," Lukman said in a statement, Saturday.
The Directorate General hosted the 11th Steering Committee Meeting for Civil Aviation Technical Cooperation alongside the DGAC in Jakarta on Wednesday, Sept. 16.
The session was attended by representatives from the DGAC, technical experts, and Airbus, led by Senior Vice President of Airbus Aviation Safety Yannick Malinge.
Lukman expressed gratitude for the ongoing commitment from DGAC and Airbus.
Key technical areas under the partnership include specific approvals for low-visibility operations, Safety Management System (SMS) assessments, risk management, personnel licensing procedures, and the refinement of Indonesia's State Safety Programme.
"Through this cooperation, we hope both civil aviation authorities can continue sharing knowledge and expertise, making our safety oversight capacity more competent, standardized, risk-based, coordinated, and sustainable," Lukman remarked.
He added that the meeting aimed to align future priorities ahead of the International Civil Aviation Organization Universal Safety Oversight Audit Programme (ICAO USOAP), expected to take place in 2027.
While the upcoming audit is a key milestone, Lukman stressed that maintaining safety oversight remains an ongoing institutional responsibility.
Thibaut Lallemand, Director of Asia-Pacific Cooperation at France's DGAC, commended the constructive progress across all priority areas, noting that the insights gained must be fully embedded to build lasting institutional capacity.

title: Menos coches y más motos en el parque móvil de la València postcovid
content:
Menos coches y más motos en el parque móvil de la València postcovid
Movilidad
La semana de la movilidad enfrenta a gobierno local y oposición en una guerra de cifras por el tráfico
Una retahíla de motocicletas, hasta 30 en una acera, yacen aparcadas en la céntrica calle Garrigues de València. En la de San Vicente hay tres aparcamientos para recarga de eléctricos, uno de ellos ocupado por una BMW, conectado en esos momentos. En las calles que bordean la plaza del Ayuntamiento se perciben casi más motocicletas que coches, en una ciudad que reordenó su tráfico en el centro hace unos años, coincidiendo con la pandemia. Desde entonces, el parque móvil de la ciudad se ha reducido un 1,8%, según los datos de la DGT en la ciudad.
De los 513.747 vehículos en 2020 se ha pasado a los 504.178: solo las motocicletas y los remolques y tractores industriales han aumentado en número. Las primeras, un 12,7%; los segundos, un 9,15%. El resto, según las cifras oficiales, han disminuido entre un 2% de los autobuses y un 24,2% de los ciclomotores. Con todo, la movilidad en la ciudad se siente menos fluida, y en ella juega un papel fundamental el área metropolitana, como bien se vio en la dana y ayer mismo: un accidente en la V-21 complicó la entrada a València a primera hora que generó tres quilómetros de retención.
Muchos trabajadores llegan en coche a la capital, como ha explicado la UPV en un reciente análisis donde asegura que desde 2022 se ha producido un incremento del tráfico en los accesos principales a la ciudad de entorno a un 5%. Clave es esta idea: prácticamente toda la población de la ciudad tiene algún servicio de movilidad a menos de cinco minutos a pie de su vivienda, pero esta desciende hasta el 46% al analizar el área metropolitana.
Sus residentes usan Cercanías o Metrovalencia, cuyos tornos permanecían ayer abiertos por el Día sin Coches. Tampoco gastaba viajes del bonobús quien viajaba con la EMT, aunque muchos ni se dieran cuenta de que la máquina advertía del “viaje gratis”. “He pasado la tarjeta, ni lo sabía”, decía una señora con el Bono Oro en la mano. Los más avispados se llevaron uno de los 500 bonobuses que el Ayuntamiento escondió en distintos autobuses y, confirmó después, que habían sido encontrados, todos, a primera hora. Los podrán usar hoy, ayer se insistía en que el día era de viaje gratuito para fomentar un transporte público muy cuestionado en los últimos años.
Compromís alega que la media diaria de vehículos se ha incrementado un 146,6% en la calle Colón desde que gobierna Catalá
Algunos conductores sabían de la sorpresa “porque lo he leído en redes sociales”, otros pasaban la mañana como siempre, evitando cargas y descargas atestadas, dobles filas -tan típicas de València- y recogiendo a viajeros. En aspecto, la de ayer fue una jornada más para el tráfico en la capital, sobre todo en su centro, que sigue obstruido por las obras de la calle Colón y cuánto esto supone para las vías aledañas.
Es uno de los motivos de enfrentamiento entre gobierno local y oposición, que afea con datos el aumento del tráfico rodado. Compromís alega que la media diaria de vehículos se ha incrementado un 146,6% en la calle Colón desde que gobiernan PP y Vox, además de señalar un aumento de quejas de usuarios de la EMT, que sitúan en un 15,9% en junio de 2026 más que en 2025 y un 7,1% en el acumulado del año, mientras que “ha cerrado 2025 con récord de viajeros y la misma flota que en 2024”. A esto, el concejal de movilidad, Jesús Carbonell, contesta que hay en marcha un plan de inversiones de 172 millones que incluye la compra de 222 autobuses y la contratación de 160 conductores; y sobre los accesos de la calle Colón, que los vehículos que ahora pasan por ahí son “los que dejan de pasar por la Gran Vía”.

title: YODAS v3: Over 1 Million Hours of High-Bandwidth, Stereophonic, Multilingual Speech
content: We present YODAS v3, a weakly-labeled speech corpus containing over 1.1 million hours of 48kHz multi-channel audio in 147 languages, released under a CC BY 3.0 license. YODAS v3 is not only the largest open speech dataset to date, but also the first truly large-scale speech corpus with high-fidelity stereo audio. We first provide the collection methodology for the corpus, where we introduce new techniques for gathering language-balanced speech data. The effectiveness of our approach is shown by the language distribution of the crawled data: 22 languages in YODAS v3 have over 10K hours and 73 languages have over 5K hours of data. We then conduct extensive analyses on the composition of the data, such as the distribution of languages, audio quality, and transcription quality. Finally, we train baseline speech recognition and neural codec models to show the effectiveness of the dataset. Download at https://huggingface.co/datasets/espnet/yodas3.

title: Provea se reúne con delegación de la AN 2015: «La agenda social debe ser prioritaria»
content:
Provea se reúne con delegación de la AN 2015: «La agenda social debe ser prioritaria»
Provea señaló como fundamental la construcción de «una ruta clara y creíble» para la reinstitucionalización del Poder Electoral, que incluya la elección de un nuevo Presidente de la República
El Programa Venezolano de Educación-Acción en Derechos Humanos (Provea) sostuvo un encuentro con la delegación negociadora de la Asamblea Nacional 2015, Dinorah Figuera. La organización presentó una serie de propuestas orientadas a la reinstitucionalización del país y demandaron que la agenda social no quede olvidada en las conversaciones con el oficialismo.
«En el marco del Diálogo para la Transición Democrática la agenda social debe ser prioritaria. Ninguno de los cambios tendrá éxito si el país no avanza en la restitución de las conquistas sociales y en el cumplimiento, por parte del Estado, de su enorme deuda social», destacó la organización.
El coordinador general de Provea, Óscar Murillo, entregó a Dinorah Figuera y su equipo una comunicación donde se subraya la urgencia de corregir las fallas estructurales que han propiciado violaciones graves a los derechos humanos, la impunidad y la denegación de justicia en el país.
«Para Venezuela es clave recuperar la separación e independencia de los poderes públicos para garantizar la estabilidad nacional. Esos primeros poderes en reconstruir deben ser el Poder Judicial y el Electoral, ambos subordinados por largo tiempo al Poder Ejecutivo y al partido de gobierno», señaló Provea en redes sociales.
*Lea también: Reforma de la ley del TSJ sale en Gaceta en medio del inicio del diálogo en Caracas
Además de la renovación de magistrados del Tribunal Supremo de Justicia, la organización abogó por la liberación de todos los presos políticos y el cierre inmediato de investigaciones y enjuiciamientos por motivos políticos.
Un genuino proceso de redemocratización, destacó Provea, debe conducir en el desmontaje del aparato represivo y del andamiaje jurídico que cercena el espacio cívico. Asimismo, se señaló como fundamental la construcción de «una ruta clara y creíble» para la reinstitucionalización del Poder Electoral, que incluya la elección de un nuevo Presidente de la República conforme a lo constitucionalmente establecido y en un plazo razonable.
La organización instó a Figuera y su equipo a incidir ante la comunidad internacional para la realización de elecciones libres y transparentes. «El único camino para rescatar la democracia y garantizar los derechos humanos de los venezolanos, pasa por escuchar y respetar la voluntad ciudadana».
*El periodismo en Venezuela se ejerce en un entorno hostil para la prensa con decenas de instrumentos jurídicos dispuestos para el castigo de la palabra, especialmente las leyes «contra el odio», «contra el fascismo» y «contra el bloqueo». Este contenido fue escrito tomando en consideración las amenazas y límites que, en consecuencia, se han impuesto a la divulgación de informaciones desde dentro del país.

title: Ethiopia’s Changing Place in the World’s Imagination
content:
Ethiopia’s Changing Place in the World’s Imagination
Addis Ababa, September 22, 2026 (FMC) – For decades, a narrow set of images came to define Ethiopia for much of the outside world: drought-stricken landscapes, famine, emergency relief, poverty and people waiting for assistance.
Those realities were never the whole country. But they became powerful shorthand for it.
Something more complicated is now emerging.
Across Ethiopia, a different collection of images is increasingly competing for attention: wheat fields stretching across irrigated lowlands, coffee moving into premium global markets, millions of seedlings planted in a single day, digital identities connecting citizens to services, new industrial and logistics infrastructure taking shape, and major energy projects altering the country’s productive capacity.
The change is not cosmetic.
It is being produced by changes in what the country is doing.
A country once associated internationally with wheat shortages is now producing wheat at a scale that has enabled exports. Ethiopia began exporting wheat internationally in 2023 after expanding irrigated production and adopting heat-tolerant varieties, turning a former import challenge into one of the most visible examples of its agricultural transformation.
Coffee offers another image of the changing economy. Ethiopia’s coffee exports generated about 2.65 billion US dollars in 2024/25, while export earnings subsequently reached a new record of three billion dollars, according to government figures.
Then there is the landscape itself.
The Green Legacy movement has transformed environmental restoration into a mass national undertaking.
Ethiopia reported planting more than 805 million seedlings in a single day during the 2026 campaign, while the cumulative number of seedlings planted since the initiative began in 2019 reached tens of billions.
The digital landscape is changing too.
Fayda, Ethiopia’s national digital identification system, has expanded to tens of millions of registrations. Digital payments, telecommunications expansion and artificial-intelligence initiatives are introducing another vocabulary into the country’s international profile—one increasingly associated with technological capacity rather than technological absence.
The physical landscape is changing alongside it.
The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam stands as the most prominent example: a nationally financed mega-project that has become central to Ethiopia’s electricity ambitions and its broader development narrative.
Around it sits a growing portfolio of infrastructure, industrial, energy, aviation and logistics projects intended to expand the productive foundations of the economy.
None of this means the older realities have disappeared.
Ethiopia continues to confront poverty, food insecurity, climate shocks, displacement and other serious challenges. Emergency needs remain real, and reducing a complex country to a story of transformation would be as incomplete as reducing it to a story of crisis.
That is precisely why the change in perception matters.
The emerging Ethiopia is not simply the opposite of the Ethiopia once portrayed through emergency imagery. It is a country containing both vulnerability and ambition, hardship and construction, unfinished problems and expanding capacity.
What is changing is the range of images available to describe it.
A wheat harvest can now sit beside a famine photograph.
A digital identity system beside a story of aid dependence.
A restored landscape beside an image of drought.
A major industrial project beside the old picture of an underdeveloped economy.
The newer images do not erase history. They complicate it.
And perhaps that is the most important transformation of all.
Ethiopia is increasingly presenting the world with more than one story to tell about it.
The country’s international image is no longer being written only through what it lacks, but increasingly through what it is producing, building, restoring, exporting and attempting to create.
The old images may remain part of Ethiopia’s history.
But they no longer have to be the only way the world sees the country.

title: Mejor vigilancia y observación: el legado científico de la erupción del volcán Tajogaite de La Palma
content:
Santa Cruz de Tenerife.- La erupción del volcán Tajogaite, en La Palma (2021) dejó un rastro de destrucción y desolación, pero también un legado científico que se traduce en un refuerzo de las capacidades de vigilancia volcánica, investigación y gestión de los peligros geofísicos.
Cuando se cumplen cinco años del inicio del proceso eruptivo, el Instituto Geográfico Nacional (IGN) destaca que desde entonces ha incorporado nuevas redes de observación, herramientas de inteligencia artificial, sistemas de modelización y nuevas líneas de trabajo en geoquímica y comunicación científica.
Gran impacto
Indica que la experiencia de la erupción tuvo «un gran impacto» dentro del Ministerio de Transportes, que optó por reformar el IGN para que los peligros geofísicos, entre los que se encuentra la actividad volcánica, estuvieran mejor articulados.
Y para ello se creó una estructura específica con una Subdirección General independiente que aborde estos peligros y «mejoró sensiblemente» las condiciones laborales del personal para adecuarlo al trabajo en emergencias, apostando por «una clara profesionalización» del personal especializado en peligros de origen geofísico.
El IGN recuerda también que junto con el Instituto Volcanológico de Canarias (Involcan) ha desarrollado ALERTA CO2, un proyecto pionero en el mundo de vigilancia de gases de origen volcánico, con más de 1.500 sensores que lo convierten en la red más densa de vigilancia de CO2 volcánico del planeta.
Más observación
La erupción del Tajogaite puso de manifiesto la necesidad de disponer de redes de observación más densas, automatizadas y capaces de proporcionar información en tiempo casi real, incide el IGN.
La red sísmica de la isla se había densificado ya en 2021 y sus datos se mantienen abiertos al público para poder ser estudiados por cualquier institución.
Para el control de deformaciones volcánicas se incrementaron las estaciones GNSS e inclinómetros, y se adquirieron imágenes InSAR del satélite PAZ hasta 2024 para generar series temporales y mapas de velocidad.
En 2021 se instaló también un gravímetro relativo que permaneció más de un año.
En geoquímica se desplegaron más de 30 sensores de CO2 desarrollados por el IGN para poder determinar el fenómeno posvolcánico de emanaciones gaseosas antes del desarrollo del proyecto ALERTA CO2.
En geología, el uso del laboratorio del Centro Geofísico de Canarias ha permitido el corte y la clasificación de las rocas por primera vez en una erupción en las islas.
Campañas de campo y análisis sísmico
Desde la erupción se han redoblado las campañas de campo: en geoquímica se inició el muestreo de fumarolas en cráteres, continuando con CO2 en pozos y manantiales, y se han incorporado campañas de flujo difuso; mientras que las campañas RTK de control de deformaciones siguen con su cadencia trimestral.
El análisis sísmico ha experimentado uno de los cambios más significativos desde entonces.
Se han establecido detectores automáticos con técnicas de aprendizaje automático para detectar y analizar de forma más rápida y homogénea la actividad sísmica.
La aplicación a los datos de la erupción generó un catálogo sísmico mucho más completo, permitiendo estudiar con mayor detalle la migración de la sismicidad y la evolución del sistema magmático. La automatización permite además afrontar episodios de elevada actividad donde el análisis manual resulta especialmente exigente, valora el IGN.
También se han desarrollado herramientas de simulación numérica de coladas de lava para análisis de escenarios y simulacros, y se ha trabajado en la automatización de avisos de aviación por emisión de cenizas.
Publicaciones
La información obtenida ha generado 18 publicaciones en revistas internacionales con participación de investigadores del IGN junto a instituciones españolas e internacionales.
Estos trabajos han avanzado en el conocimiento de la estructura profunda del sistema magmático de La Palma, la evolución de sismicidad y deformación, la dinámica eruptiva y la relación entre observables geofísicos y geoquímicos.
La investigación más reciente integra datos petrológicos, geoquímicos y geofísicos para reconstruir los procesos preeruptivos y sineruptivos de la erupción de 2021 en Cumbre Vieja. EFE

title: Florida used robot rabbits to hunt Burmese pythons threatening the Everglades
content:
Florida used an unusual tool to control the growing population of invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades: solar-powered robot rabbits. In 2025, the South Florida Water Management District and the University of Florida teamed up to deploy robotic rabbit decoys designed to mimic real prey and lure pythons out of hiding using artificial intelligence (AI), heat signatures and scent simulation.
The robots are part of Florida’s broader effort to remove Burmese pythons, which have disrupted native wildlife populations across the state. The devices use AI-powered cameras to detect approaching snakes and alert officials, who can then send trained python removal agents to capture and remove them. The technology is being used alongside the annual Florida Python Challenge and other removal programmes, not replacing them.
How Florida’s AI-powered robot rabbits work
The solar-powered robots are designed to imitate prey that Burmese pythons hunt. They produce a heat signature and emit a scent intended to attract the snakes, which use thermal sensing and smell while hunting. Each robot has an AI-powered camera that monitors the surrounding area. When it detects a python approaching, the system alerts South Florida Water Management District officials. A trained python removal agent can then be dispatched to the location.
The district and University of Florida are deploying the robots at sites across South Florida where pythons are known to hide. The approach is intended to help monitor areas that can be difficult to survey using conventional methods.
“These innovative robots produce a heat signature and emit a smell designed to attract pythons. The robots are equipped with cameras that monitor for pythons and notify District officials when a snake is detected. Once notified, the District can dispatch a python removal agent to the area,” the district noted.
Why Florida is targeting Burmese pythons
Burmese pythons were introduced into the Everglades during the 1970s and have since become an invasive predator in Florida. Researchers estimate that between 100,000 and 300,000 Burmese pythons are present across the state’s subtropical regions. The snakes can grow longer than 18 feet, and adult females can lay more than 70 eggs in a single clutch. Their presence has affected native mammals, birds and reptiles, reducing available prey for species including Florida panthers, bobcats and birds of prey.
A 2012 US Geological Survey study found that raccoon and opossum populations in parts of the Everglades had declined by nearly 99% following the spread of Burmese pythons.
Florida Python Challenge adds to python removal efforts
Florida has also relied on trained contractors and public participation to remove Burmese pythons. The annual Florida Python Challenge brings professional and amateur hunters together for a 10-day competition, and participants must complete a safety course before taking part. In the 2026 challenge, 907 participants from 30 states, as well as Vietnam and Canada, collectively removed 280 Burmese pythons. The competition's overall tally has now exceeded 1,600 snakes.
Tom Rahill won the $10,000 grand prize after removing 96 snakes, while Rahm Levinson received $1,000 for capturing the longest python, measuring 16 feet, five inches. Additional prizes were awarded across professional, novice and military categories.
“The number of invasive pythons removed from the Everglades during the 2026 Florida Python Challenge is a major victory for Florida’s native wildlife and a testament to what can be accomplished through strong partnerships and public participation,” FWC chairman Rodney Barreto said in a statement.
Since 2017, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and South Florida Water Management District contractors have removed more than 19,000 snakes. The district's robotic rabbit programme is intended to add another method to those ongoing efforts.

title: Development and Internal Validation of a Nomogram for Delayed Treatment in Pediatric Testicular Torsion: A Retrospective Study Spanning Over Two Decades.
content: Testicular torsion (TT) is a time-sensitive pediatric urologic emergency in which delayed treatment markedly reduces the likelihood of testicular salvage. This study aimed to identify factors associated with delayed treatment in children with TT and to develop and internally validate a nomogram for retrospective characterization of delay-risk profiles. A total of 540 pediatric patients with surgically confirmed TT were retrospectively included and randomly assigned to a training cohort (n=377) and a validation cohort (n=163). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for variable selection in the training cohort, followed by multivariable logistic regression to construct the final model and nomogram. Model performance was evaluated by discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis (DCA), and bootstrap internal validation. Nine predictors were retained for final model development: age, sports or injuries, persistent symptoms, onset during sleep, misdiagnosis, degree of cord twisting > 180°, guardian awareness of TT, transfer distance, and ipsilateral hydrocele. The nomogram showed good discrimination, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.952 (95% CI, 0.932-0.973) in the training cohort and 0.940 (95% CI, 0.904-0.976) in the validation cohort. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities. DCA indicated potential net benefit in both cohorts. To our knowledge, this study developed the first nomogram for retrospectively characterizing delay-risk profiles in children with TT. Internal validation showed good retrospective discrimination within the study cohorts. This nomogram may help identify clinical and care-pathway patterns relevant to quality improvement.

title: Il viaggio dimenticato delle sedonere: le donne della Valcellina che sfidarono le montagne con un carretto raccontate in un docufilm
content:
Il viaggio dimenticato delle sedonere: le donne della Valcellina che sfidarono le montagne con un carretto raccontate in un docufilm
C’è un’immagine che sembra arrivare da un altro tempo: donne coi fazzoletti a riparare la testa, carretti tirati da mani nude, la strada davanti e chilometri da percorrere. Dietro, alle loro spalle, una valle, una casa, una famiglia e, davanti, un mondo del tutto sconosciuto. Erano le sedonere, le donne delle montagne friulane che tra la fine dell’Ottocento e la prima metà del Novecento hanno lasciato i paesi dell’alta Valcellina, ai confini con il Vajont, per scendere verso la pianura e le città del Nord Italia. A cercare fortuna.
A raccogliere questa fragile memoria è FORA PAL MONT – I passi rimasti (Fora pal mont è letteralmente “fuori per il mondo, in giro per il mondo”, ndr), l’ultimo documentario diretto da Lorena Trevisan e Michele Pastrello, che incontra sei delle donne che hanno vissuto quella stagione e che oggi, tra i novanta e i cento anni, raccontano in prima persona il viaggio delle sedonere. Le loro voci riportano alla luce un pezzo di storia rimasto a lungo ai margini: quello di donne che, partendo dalla montagna, hanno attraversato l’Italia e conquistato spazi di autonomia in un’epoca in cui il loro ruolo era ancora fortemente limitato.
Con sé avevano decine di manufatti e oggetti di legno, soprattutto i sedon (i mestoli e gli utensili da cucina, da cui deriva il loro nome), e li vendevano lungo il cammino. Partivano per settimane, a volte per mesi, e dormivano dove capitava: nei fienili, nelle stalle, presso le famiglie che offrivano loro un posto per la notte. Nessun viaggio romantico, quindi, ma fatica allo stato puro mista a freddo e solitudine e partenze che nascevano dalla necessità. Le comunità di montagna erano povere, isolate, con poche possibilità di lavoro e così, il denaro guadagnato dalle sedonere serviva a sostenere l’economia familiare e a portare qualcosa in più nelle case.
Eppure, quei viaggi produssero un effetto inatteso. Per molte donne, infatti, raccontano Pastrello e Trevisan, rappresentarono il primo spazio di autonomia fuori dai confini del paese natale. Lontane dalle vicissitudini di una comunità, imparavano strade nuove, incontravano persone diverse, gestivano denaro, prendevano decisioni. In un’epoca in cui il ruolo femminile era spesso confinato alla famiglia e alla casa, una sedonera era una donna che camminava da sola nel mondo. Una lavoratrice, una commerciante, una figura che oggi potremmo definire indipendente, ma che allora veniva semplicemente considerata una necessità della vita.
Hanno fatto tanto per se stesse e per la valle – spiega Lorena Trevisan -, inconsapevoli di essere state piccola parte attiva di un processo di cambiamento culturale. Ed è proprio per questo che le loro testimonianze sono ancora così contemporanee, soprattutto per noi donne. Ci ricordano che l’emancipazione non è qualcosa che è cominciato un giorno grazie a una singola persona, ma è un percorso costruito da molte persone e da più ceti sociali, fatto di tante piccole libertà conquistate, spesso senza nemmeno chiamarle così. Ed è un percorso ancora in divenire. Le loro storie partivano dalla valle, tanto tempo fa, ma in un certo senso arrivano ancora fino a noi.
Una storia rimasta ai margini
Come tante storie di donne del Novecento, anche quella delle sedonere è rimasta per lungo tempo ai margini della memoria collettiva. La sociologa Casimira Grandi ha usato l’espressione “presenza assente” per descrivere proprio questa condizione: donne fondamentali nella vita economica e sociale delle comunità, ma spesso poco presenti nei racconti ufficiali, negli archivi e nella narrazione storica.
Le sedonere c’erano. Hanno lavorato e contribuito alla sopravvivenza delle loro famiglie e dei loro paesi, ma il loro viaggio è rimasto quasi invisibile.
Le donne lavoravano nei campi, con gli animali, in casa e in molte attività integrative – racconta Pastrello -,pur con diritti fortemente limitati tanto è vero che fino al 1919 vigeva l’autorizzazione maritale. La Prima guerra mondiale, per forza di cose, rese più visibile il loro ruolo economico, ma il fascismo ricondusse presto la donna al modello ideologico di moglie e madre, limitandone ambizioni, formazione e carriera. Ancora nel 1931 una larghissima percentuale di donne veniva classificata nelle statistiche con il fumoso “attendenti a casa”. È in questa contraddizione che si inserisce la storia delle sedonere di Fora Pal Mont. Erano donne ambulanti che svolgevano un mestiere percepito come maschile, viaggiavano tantissimo chi trainando un carretto ed altre con ingombranti cassettiere, dormivano sotto le stelle. Si sentivano commercianti, anche se difficilmente potevano rivendicare apertamente quel ruolo. Nel Nord Italia esistono pochissimi casi analoghi di lavoro ambulante femminile organizzato su questa scala.
Il documentario che restituisce voce alle ultime sedonere
Il docufilm – sulle note di Fémene (del cantautore Franco Giordani su poesia della poetessa Bianca Borsatti) – incontra sei delle ultime sedonere – Teresa, Luigia, Vittorina, Fiorina, Luciana, Carolina (la più giovane ha 91 anni, Luigia ne ha 102) – che attraverso i loro racconti riportano alla luce quel mondo fatto di fatica, coraggio, ironia e resistenza. Sono storie di donne che hanno attraversato un’Italia diversa: quella delle valli isolate, delle famiglie numerose, del lavoro manuale e delle partenze senza sapere sempre cosa avrebbe aspettato loro dall’altra parte della montagna. Nei loro racconti c’è la durezza del viaggio, ma anche il ricordo di una libertà conquistata passo dopo passo.
La storia delle sedonere appartiene a un territorio preciso, l’alta Valcellina, ma vuole parlare di tutte quelle donne che hanno lavorato senza essere chiamate “lavoratrici”, che hanno sostenuto economie familiari senza comparire nei libri, che hanno modificato lentamente le proprie comunità senza entrare nei racconti ufficiali.
Ed è questa la domanda che il documentario ci lascia: quante storie di donne abbiamo perso perché nessuno si è fermato ad ascoltarle?
FORA PAL MONT – I passi rimasti ha iniziato nel 2026 il suo percorso nei festival e nelle rassegne italiane: è stato selezionato da Le Giornate della Luce presso Cinemazero di Pordenone, Nuovi Mondi Film Festival, Edera Film Festival di Treviso come evento speciale, Mario Puzo Film Festival ed ETNOfilmFest di Este. Ha inoltre ricevuto la Menzione d’Onore della Giuria al Premio Vittorio De Seta 2026.

title: Opinion: Social media bans are passing around the world. How will we know if they help teens?
content:
In December 2025, as social media’s potential impact on youth mental health faced growing scrutiny, Australia became the first country to ban social media for people under 16, with Indonesia quickly following. The European Union is taking a slightly different approach, banning social media for children under 13 and personal accounts for people under 15 after pressure from several E.U. nations.
Elsewhere, big tech companies are being challenged in the courts. Meta recently agreed to pay up to $18 billion to resolve claims in the U.S. that Facebook and Instagram harmed children. Meta will also introduce “safety by design” features for young people, such as concealing the number of “likes” on posts. But will these features meaningfully change young people’s behavior or experiences online? Will the bans have their intended effect?
With major changes being introduced around the world, researchers must seize this opportunity to conduct robust independent evaluations of how social media — and its regulation — impacts teenagers’ mental health, wellbeing and social lives. With almost half of all mental health problems emerging by the age of 18, this research is crucial.
One size might not fit all
Ultimately, the question is not simply whether social media is inherently “good” or “bad,” or whether restrictions “work” or “don’t work.” Instead, researchers need to look at whether changing young people’s digital environments leads to meaningful changes in their mental health and wellbeing.
The evidence increasingly suggests that there is unlikely to be a single “social media effect” that impacts all teenagers in the same way.
Social media restrictions will likely affect individual young people differently, based on factors such as their age, whether they have existing mental health problems, and their sleep patterns. It could have different effects based on teenagers’ gender, their socioeconomic background, or where they live (for example, whether they come from an urban or rural area).
Social media can be an important source of community, so restrictions may affect people from marginalized backgrounds in different ways, including those who identify as LGBTQ+. It will most likely also depend on the specific way that a person uses (or previously used) a given platform.
If restrictions do bring changes in teenagers’ mental health, researchers need to understand the mechanisms behind the change. For example, if some young people experience an improvement in their mental health following the restrictions, might it be because they are meeting up more with friends in real life, or are they getting more sleep? The answer to the why question could shape future policies that support youth mental health.
Lessons from Australia
Early findings from Australia suggest that age verification from social media companies is a significant challenge in implementing the ban.
An evaluation published in the British Medical Journal found little evidence of substantial reductions in social media use three months after Australia implemented its ban. It found that many young people were continuing to use restricted platforms and finding ways around age-verification systems. Meanwhile, a report by Australia’s online watchdog found that more than 80% of children were still using a restricted online platform.
Behavioral economist Leonardo Bursztyn and colleagues found that many teenagers continued to believe their peers were using restricted platforms and reported they would be more willing to stop if more of their peers stopped, too. This shows the importance of peer influence in adolescent decision-making, which will be a factor in the restrictions globally.
The difficulties in implementing the ban in Australia mean that it is still too early to say whether it has improved young people’s mental health and in what ways it has worked. Still, this raises an important point that implementation will be a major factor across the world.
Assessing the change in the U.K.
In the U.K., the government is planning to introduce a social media ban in spring 2027.
I work at Wellcome, a global philanthropic foundation based in London and one of the biggest funders of mental health research in the world. We are going to be funding evaluations of the impact of the social media ban in the U.K. on youth mental health, with research teams working with tens of thousands of teenagers. All our work is guided by young people with experience in both social media use and mental health problems, so that research best reflects their concerns.
In this case, we consulted with a group of young people to ask for advice on how best to design and implement the research on social media restrictions. The young people reframed the whole debate. Rather than focusing solely on whether social media is harmful and whether we need a ban, they repeatedly asked us to look at what role social media currently plays in young people’s lives — and what might replace it if access is restricted.
Young people are not oblivious about the risks of social media, such as misinformation and harmful content, but they also recognize it as infrastructure for learning, connection, support, creativity, and belonging. They highlighted that evaluating the restrictions requires understanding how teenagers’ time is otherwise spent. For example, they said, researchers should look at whether young people are spending time in a positive way by cultivating outdoor hobbies, friendships, sleeping better, and studying more. Or will they simply spend the time being bored, or find themselves in unregulated online spaces?
In short, the young people were asking researchers to evaluate changes in their lives, rather than simply looking at changes in their screen time.
They suggested that the evaluation should not only focus on how to reduce harm, but also on understanding what kinds of social environments best support young people’s mental health and wellbeing.
A global opportunity
We are not simply trying to evaluate the U.K. government’s policy on banning social media. We are trying to understand a much broader and fundamental question: How do changes in the digital environment impact young people’s mental health and wellbeing, and why?
While we are focusing on the U.K., this is a globally relevant question. Comparing what happens in Australia and the U.K., with the results in the E.U., where they will be cracking down on certain practices, and elsewhere in the world, via Meta’s new tools, will be illuminating. Perhaps we will end up learning that bans are the solution. Perhaps some tools will be more effective than others.
There is a seismic opportunity for research teams around the world to join forces to evaluate how social media and its restrictions impact youth mental health. The answers that emerge could influence how we intervene in youth mental health for generations to come.
Camilla Iannone is research lead in the mental health evidence team at Wellcome.

title: Freedom: A Difficult Path That Comes at Women’s Cost
content:
I grew up in a house with mud walls and a low ceiling. From the small window of my room, I would always look at the sky over Kabul, a sky that seemed to me like a vast canvas. In a city that sometimes smelled of fear and insecurity, I had learned to seek refuge in the world of books. To me, every book was a window opening into another world, a world where no wall could stop the human mind from taking flight.
This is the story of a girl who had ambitious dreams but was buried and forgotten. In one of the remote provinces, where harmful traditions sometimes overshadow basic human principles, Zahra was a girl whose dreams were confined by the mud walls of her home. In that society, both hidden and open violence had taken root not only in the streets and markets but also in major family decisions.
Zahra’s father, under pressure from harmful social customs and in an attempt to resolve a long-standing dispute, decided to marry her off to a man many years older than her. Zahra, who dreamed of continuing her education and gaining knowledge, resisted the forced decision. But in a society where structural violence had deprived girls of the right to choose, her voice was lost amid the demands of the men making the decisions. Her father viewed marriage through misguided interpretations of tradition, not as a union based on consent and human dignity, but as a means of protecting his own “honor.”
On the day of the marriage ceremony, Zahra, her eyes red from hidden tears, witnessed a transaction in which her human dignity was disregarded. What she experienced was nothing less than the loss of her sense of self and freedom.
The marriage not only distanced Zahra from her dreams but also pushed her into a cycle of loneliness and despair. In a society where family relationships are shaped by violence and coercion, Zahra, living silently in her new home and enduring violence from her husband, was no longer the cheerful and ambitious girl she once was.
Then, one morning, the devastating news came: “Zahra had taken her own life.” Hearing those words, I trembled all over. What injustice had she suffered? Why had that intelligent girl reached such a desperate point? Why had she been forced into such a fate?
During those days, my only source of comfort was the small library I had in a corner of our home. With her limited education, my mother taught me that knowledge was not simply about reading words, but about gaining a deeper understanding of life. She always told me that instead of becoming consumed by the bitter side of life, I should search for its deeper meaning.
Kabul was a city of contradictions for me. Alongside poverty and hardship, there were still people who, despite living in poverty, had generous hearts and helped others. From them, I learned that humanity is not measured by wealth, but by the greatness of one’s spirit. This was one of life’s greatest lessons, one I learned from ordinary people in the city’s streets and alleys.
When the schools were closed, I did not lose hope. I told myself, “If the school is closed, my mind is still open.” I began writing. For me, writing was not a hobby, but a “silent uprising.” I wrote so I would not forget who I was or what I dreamed of. I wrote so that I could be the voice of all the girls who, in silence, were searching for a path toward the light.
During those difficult days, I thought about why human rights are sometimes disregarded in the country. I found the answer in “illiteracy” and “lack of awareness.” When a society moves away from knowledge, superstition and harmful traditions can take the place of truth. I decided to become part of that change. I did not want to be just a passive observer. I wanted to be someone who could use her pen to break down the walls of ignorance.
I thought about the value of informed marriage based on love and respect. A marriage in which two people come together as companions to build a dignified life, rather than as owner and owned. In Islam and its teachings centered on human dignity, mutual consent and respect for the dignity of both women and men are fundamental principles. I knew that if a society wanted to progress, it needed to return to these human principles.
Every morning when I woke up, I asked myself, “What will I learn today?” I began learning new skills. I wanted to become a woman who, when she entered society, would not only have something to say but would also know how to help address the problems facing her community.
Sometimes I was afraid of the insecurity in the city. But now, when I think about those days, I realize that freedom is not a gift; it is an achievement. Freedom is born in the moment when you decide that instead of giving in to sorrow, you will learn to give hope to others. I am no longer that frightened girl. I have become like the wind, finding its way through the rocks. I know that after every sunset, another sunrise will come.
Perhaps Kabul is a city of fear today, but I still believe in the dawn of liberation. Amid all this destruction, I stand and build. I have learned that even if the whole world stands against me, as long as I believe in myself, no wall can silence my voice. I am still moving forward, with fear and limitations, but with a heart that beats for freedom and awareness.

title: Replicating the Geometry of Emotion Representations in a Base Open-Weights Model
content: Sofroniew et al. (2026) report that emotion concepts in Claude Sonnet 4.5 are represented as vectors whose geometry mirrors human affect psychology. We replicate the representational core of that study on the base pretrained model google/gemma-2-27b, inheriting every disclosed parameter, resolving unspecified steps by disclosed rules, and changing only the subject model. From 205,200 newly generated Claude Sonnet 4.5 stories matching the original corpus design, we extract 171 emotion vectors and recover the core results. The leading principal components form an affective circumplex (PC1 carries 26.7% of variance against the original study's ~27%, PC2 13.4% against ~14%), emotions cluster into similar intuitive families, and the geometry holds across a broad late-middle band. The valence axis aligns with human norms (r = 0.72, against 0.81) and is stable across scales and depth. Arousal aligns at r = 0.67 (against 0.66) but only at the full 171-emotion scale and late depth, so we do not classify it as replicated. Extending the original analysis, a 46-layer sweep locates a sharp seam at L22-26, where the geometry consolidates and the vocabulary readout becomes legible. An embedding-layer baseline finds much of the geometry already present in the static token embeddings, with arousal as the exception. On top-activating held-out text, the geometry predicts token-level co-activation at r = 0.907. At least 52% of vectors peak on structurally non-conceptual tokens, a measured floor for max-activation confounds. Even when a document contains the vector's emotion word, the peak lands on that word only 6.1% of the time. Because the subject is a base model and the stimuli are Claude-generated fiction, the recovered structure is a property of the pretrained representation of Claude-rendered emotion. The original's causal and assistant-facing analyses are out of scope. Code and data are released.

title: MML culmina intervención en río Lurín tras retirar 9000 m³ de maleza y material rocoso
content:
La Municipalidad Metropolitana de Lima (MML) culminó los trabajos de reducción del riesgo de desastres en el río Lurín, donde retiró 9000 metros cúbicos de maleza y material rocoso acumulados en el cauce, a la altura del puente Pachacámac, informó la entidad edilicia.


La intervención comprendió aproximadamente 300 metros, distribuidos en 150 metros aguas arriba y 150 metros aguas abajo del puente, en un sector próximo a la carretera Panamericana Sur y a la desembocadura del río.
Con maquinaria propia y operadores de la Gerencia de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres, se realizaron labores de limpieza, descolmatación y encauzamiento, además de la conformación de un dique seco. Estas acciones permiten mantener despejado el cauce y facilitar el libre flujo del agua ante un eventual incremento del caudal.
Los trabajos contribuyen a reducir el riesgo de afectaciones en el puente Pachacámac, la infraestructura vial y las zonas cercanas.
Intervención continúa en el río Chillón
Como parte de las acciones preventivas en las principales cuencas de Lima Metropolitana, la Municipalidad de Lima continúa trabajando en el río Chillón, donde interviene un tramo de aproximadamente 4 kilómetros, desde aguas abajo del puente Trapiche hasta el puente Huatocay.
Para estas labores se han desplegado 12 maquinarias que ejecutan trabajos de limpieza, descolmatación, encauzamiento y conformación de diques.
Las acciones buscan retirar los sedimentos, maleza y otros elementos acumulados que puedan obstaculizar el paso del agua y generar puntos vulnerables ante el incremento del caudal.
La Municipalidad de Lima señaló que mantiene maquinaria y personal desplegados en las principales cuencas de la capital para ejecutar acciones preventivas que permitan reducir riesgos y proteger a la población y la infraestructura frente a posibles emergencias.
